newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP minerals unit sees few weak assets.
newsitem.headline: BHP minerals unit sees few weak assets.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday its minerals unit had fewer underperforming assets than the rest of the mining and energy group.

Asked what percentage of assets in the minerals division had a return on capital of below 10 percent, BHP Minerals chief executive Dick Carter told Reuters: "It would be under 10 percent. The ones that we have that are earning less than 10 percent are things that are in the start-up mode."
Earlier, BHP managing director John Prescott told reporters that about 10 percent of the group's asset base was underperforming and that poor assets would be put up for sale.
Carter said the mineral unit's Tasmananian Manganese smelter operation was not for sale.

"If you look at TEMCO (Tasmanian Electro Metallurgical Co) as a stand-alone activity, as often as not, it doesn't earn 10 percent -- you have to look at it as a conduit for getting manganese ore units into the market," Carter said.
The TEMCO smelter at Bell Bay in Tasmania processes manganese ore from the company's GEMCO (Groote Eylandt Mining Co) mine on Groote Eylandt off the Northern Territory, to produce ferro-alloys.
If TEMCO was considered as a vertically integrated business with the GEMCO Manganese mine then it consistently had a return on capital of greater than 15 percent, he said.
Earlier, Prescott said BHP was not going to "protect and defend businesses just because they are vertically integrated with something else."
